condition: Cauda equina syndrome presenting as urinary retention
summary: 52-year-old woman with back pain after lifting presents with painless urinary retention (950 mL), saddle numbness and lax anal tone.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Unable to pass urine since this morning
inputs.hpi: Hurt her back lifting 3 days ago. Since this morning she cannot pass urine but it is not painful. On direct questioning her bottom feels numb when wiping and her bowels have not opened. Some pain in both legs. No previous urinary problems.

exam.abdomen: Palpable, non-tender bladder. PR: lax anal tone, reduced perianal sensation.
exam.neuro: Reduced pinprick S3–S5, ankle reflexes absent bilaterally, power normal.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Cauda equina syndrome with urinary retention (CES-R)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Painless urinary retention (950 mL) with saddle anaesthesia and lax anal tone after a back injury: CES-R. Catheterise, emergency MRI, immediate spinal surgery referral.

guideline.name: SBNS/BASS — Standards of care for investigation and management of cauda equina syndrome
guideline.section: Suspected CES (bilateral radicular pain, saddle sensory change, bladder/bowel/sexual dysfunction): emergency MRI; immediate discussion with the on-call spinal surgical team; decompression as soon as possible; do not wait for urinary retention (retention indicates CES-R); post-void residual bladder scan as part of assessment
guideline.citation: Society of British Neurological Surgeons & British Association of Spine Surgeons. Standards of care for investigation and management of cauda equina syndrome. 2018. See also: GIRFT National Suspected Cauda Equina Syndrome Pathway, 2023.

rationale: Painless retention in a woman with back pain is CES until proven otherwise: MRI and spinal surgery, not an alpha-blocker and TWOC (SBNS/BASS 2018).
